Implement separate repositories for Customers and Orders data to provide controlled and consistent access to client and order information. (Repository) Provides a centralized abstraction to access and manage data from databases, encapsulating data access logic and allowing clients to interact with data sources in a consistent manner.

Use the Gateway to route requests to the appropriate services or repositories managing client and order data. (Gateway) Acts as a single entry point that routes client requests to appropriate backend services or components.

Deploy an API Gateway to expose and manage APIs for accessing client and order data services. (Api Gateway) A specialized Gateway pattern tailored for API management, providing request routing, composition, and protocol translation for microservices.

Implement a dedicated API Gateway to manage all HTTP/REST requests from PC and mobile clients, routing them to appropriate microservices. (Api Gateway) A server that acts as an API front-end, receiving API requests, enforcing throttling and security policies, passing requests to the back-end service, and then passing the response back to the requester.

Decompose the monolithic system into microservices for Customers, Orders, Delivery & Routing, Statistics, Incidents, and integrate with external Payments service. (Microservices) An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled services, each implementing business capabilities.

Implement separate backend services for PC and mobile clients if client-specific API tailoring is needed beyond what the API Gateway provides. (Backend For Frontend) Creates separate backend services tailored to the needs of different client types (e.g., PC and mobile), optimizing the API for each client.

Implement two optimization algorithms as separate strategy classes and let the delivery module select the appropriate strategy based on delay or other criteria. (Strategy) Defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable. Strategy lets the algorithm vary independently from clients that use it.
Implement optimization algorithms as plugins to the microkernel core. (Microkernel) Separates a minimal functional core from extended functionality and plugins.
Use gateway to route requests but not for algorithm implementation. (Gateway) Acts as a single entry point for multiple services, handling requests and routing them appropriately.

Implement retry logic in the OrderManager or client to limit order placement attempts to a configured maximum. (Retry) Automatically retries failed operations up to a maximum number of attempts to handle transient failures.

Implement an Adapter module that wraps the external Payments service API, exposing a consistent interface to the rest of the system. (Adapter) The Adapter pattern allows the system to interface with an external component by converting its interface into one expected by the system, enabling integration without modifying existing code.

Use a Gateway to route payment-related requests to the external Payments service. (Gateway) The Gateway pattern acts as a single entry point to a set of services, managing communication and routing requests.

Deploy an API Gateway to manage all external API calls, including those to the Payments service. (Api Gateway) An API Gateway is a server that acts as an API front-end, handling requests, routing them to appropriate services, and aggregating responses.

Create a Facade to provide a simplified interface to the Payments module internally. (Facade) The Facade pattern provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem, hiding its complexity from clients.

Implement separate microservices for Customers and Orders modules, each exposing REST APIs for CRUD operations and order processing. (Microservices) An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled services, each implementing a specific business capability.

Use repositories within each microservice to manage data access to SQL databases for Customers and Orders. (Repository) A pattern that mediates between the domain and data mapping layers, acting like an in-memory collection of domain objects.

Implement CRUD operations in the Customers and Orders microservices to manage personal data and orders. (Crud) A pattern focusing on Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations for managing data entities.

Deploy an API Gateway to route requests from clients to the appropriate Customers and Orders microservices. (Api Gateway) A server that acts as an API front-end, receiving API requests, enforcing throttling and security policies, passing requests to the back-end service, and then returning the response.

Implement Statistics and Incidents as separate microservices to encapsulate their functionality and allow independent scaling and deployment. (Microservices) An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled services, each implementing business capabilities.

Use an API Gateway to route requests to the Statistics and Incidents microservices, providing a unified interface to clients. (Gateway) A single entry point that routes client requests to appropriate backend services, often handling cross-cutting concerns like authentication, rate limiting, and load balancing.

Implement a facade to aggregate statistics and incidents data if clients require a unified simplified interface beyond the Gateway. (Facade) Provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem, hiding its internal complexity from clients.

Use observer pattern internally within microservices to propagate relevant state changes to statistics and incidents modules if real-time updates are needed. (Observer) Defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified and updated automatically.

Adopt event sourcing for critical modules like incidents to maintain a reliable history of events and support complex analytics. (Event Sourcing) Stores state changes as a sequence of events, allowing reconstruction of current state by replaying events.
